title: Normalization and finite-Tor inputs for affine integration
statement:
Fix a finite purity setting $P$, with finite coefficient ring $A=P.Coefficient$, exponent $N=P.diagonalExponent$ and the canonical ordered shifted Tate coefficients and ordinary-etale arrows of [def-sp-nested-affine-formula-data]. For every affine $k$-scheme $B$, structure map $a_B$ of finite type, and $m\ge0$, the inverse diagonal orientation of $p_m:T_m(B)\to B$ equals gammaUnit. The object $p_m^!A_B$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. For every bounded constructible finite-Tor $H$ on $B$, $p_m^*H\otimes A(m)[2m]$ and $p_m^!H$ are bounded constructible finite-Tor, and
$$\Gamma_{m,H}=\theta_{p_m,H}(1_{p_m^*H}\otimes\Gamma_{m,A_B}).$$
At $m=0$, composing gamma at $H$ with the exceptional-identity and pullback-identity comparisons gives zeroSource at $H$. gammaUnit in rank zero is the inverse of those identity comparisons at $A_B$. These clauses mean exactly NormalizedInputs P, with the fixed coefficient-unit constraints of that definition, including empty schemes.

proof.text: Apply projection-purity-agreement in the canonical finite-site presentation at every constructible finite-Tor ordinary input. Its tensor, pullback and exceptional comparison squares preserve the published counits. Reflect its equality back to ordinary arrows by full faithfulness of the finite-site comparison.

Expand smooth purity as tensor of the pullback identity and the inverse orientation followed by theta. At the coefficient unit, dualizingTensor_unit removes the tensor and unit constraints, identifying the actual inverse diagonal orientation with gammaUnit. Substitute this equality in the formula at general H.

The coefficient unit has Tor interval [0,0]. Ordinary exceptional finite-Tor preservation supplies the dualizing and exceptional targets. Pullback preserves the Tor interval, tensor with the locally free shifted Tate line preserves finite Tor amplitude and constructibility, and its even shift translates the interval. These are the ordinary APIs underlying the preservation and chart-domain lemmas; no flatness of H or omega is assumed.

In rank zero the ordered integration is the identity adjunction and its coefficient trace is the identity. The exceptional identity, exact pullback identity and right-unit comparisons in zeroSource are precisely the remaining factors of its transpose. At the coefficient unit the same cancellation gives the final gammaUnit equation, also over the empty scheme.
